title: `prompts/get`
description: Resolves one prompt with arguments into a list of messages, each with a role and a content block.
question: Can the agent resolve a prompt into messages it can actually send?
why: A prompt is only useful once it is expanded. This row is where a framework either produces messages in its own conversation format or hands back a structure the caller has to translate by hand.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers publishing this. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no prompt methods; `prompts/get` is never sent.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `MCPTool.get_prompt` returns the expanded messages joined into one string; the text survives and each message's role is dropped.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServer` interface has no prompts method, so there is no route to `prompts/get`.
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` has no prompts method; `prompts/get` is reachable only by hand through the generic `request()`.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `prompts/get` is unreachable.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `prompts/get`.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`, and the `ClientSession` lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` has no prompts API (no list, get or loader for prompts), so there is no route to `prompts/get`.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `beeai_framework.tools.mcp` has `MCPTool` only. `MCPTool.from_client` lists and wraps tools, and BeeAI has no MCP resource or prompt API.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `GetPrompt` on.
